abstract: The Theory of Sustainable Economic Convergence is a foundational theoretical work within the H Heuristics Polycrisis Resilience Series, based on the concept developed by Hunter Hughes, Founder of H Heuristics (https://polycrisisresilience.hheuristics.com/).

keyFindings.title: Conventional neoclassical and structuralist growth theories omit environmental feedback and compounding systemic risk—causing catch-up models to misprice fossil lock-in and ecological drag.

The Theory of Sustainable Economic Convergence unites five dimensions—Economic Convergence, Technological Convergence, Structural Transformation, Environmental Sustainability, and Development Resilience—lifting the Convergence Index from 39.0 (2025) to 70.5 (2050) and 91.0 (2100).

By decoupling growth from carbon and particulate pollution (-93.5% intensity by 2100), emerging economies reach 85.5% of OECD GDP per capita and 88.0% of frontier TFP while shifting 89.0% of output into high-value clean sectors.

Integrating all five dimensions yields a 12.0x 25-year social benefit-cost ratio (versus 1.7x for carbon-intensive subsidy growth) and connects directly to H Heuristics' Polycrisis Resilience and Optimizing Humanity's Outlook programs.
